name: E-MANTRA
description: Election misinformation threatens democratic discourse not only by spreading false claims but also by using rhetorical tactics that manipulate trust, emotion, identity, and interpretation. This thesis presents E-MANTRA (Election-based Manipulation Annotation for Narrative Tactic Recognition and Analysis), a framework for classify- ing the dominant manipulation tactic in election-related misinformation. Grounded in DEPICT, a six-tactic taxonomy covering Discrediting, Emotion, Polarization, Imper- sonation, Conspiracy, and Trolling, the research constructs a 900-item reference-label dataset using repeated large language model (LLM) labeling, stability filtering, and label-aware single-reviewer validation on a subset, then evaluates GPT-3.5, Llama 3-70B, Mistral-Small, DeepSeek-R1, and Phi-4, with Phi-4-mini included in auxiliary semantic-consistency analysis. Results show that in-context prompting provides the strongest reference-label construction strategy, while performance varies substantially by tactic. The thesis argues that manipulation-aware classification is designed to sup- port human-reviewed election-security workflows by shifting analysis from whether a claim is true to how it attempts to influence democratic discourse.
